MUSIC AND DANCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #14
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: MUSIC AND DANCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Best practice when working on Instrumental Transpositions: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Instrumental Transpositions with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Damage equipment used for Instrumental Transpositions.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Instrumental Transpositions.
   D. Disrupt classmates during Instrumental Transpositions.

2. Best practice when working on Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World.
   C. Practise Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   D. Refuse all feedback on Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World.

3. In music, tempo refers to: (1 mark)
   A. The ticket price
   B. Only the costume
   C. Only the volume
   D. The speed of the music

4. Best practice when working on Four-Part Harmony: (1 mark)
   A. Refuse all feedback on Four-Part Harmony.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Four-Part Harmony.
   C. Damage equipment used for Four-Part Harmony.
   D. Practise Four-Part Harmony with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

5. Best practice when working on Rhythm: (1 mark)
   A. Refuse all feedback on Rhythm.
   B. Practise Rhythm with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   C. Disrupt classmates during Rhythm.
   D. Damage equipment used for Rhythm.

6. Best practice when working on Dance Production: (1 mark)
   A. Disrupt classmates during Dance Production.
   B. Practise Dance Production with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Dance Production.
   D. Damage equipment used for Dance Production.

7. Best practice when working on Music Notation Software.: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Music Notation Software. with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Refuse all feedback on Music Notation Software..
   C. Disrupt classmates during Music Notation Software..
   D. Damage equipment used for Music Notation Software..

8. Best practice when working on Western Ensembles: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Western Ensembles with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Western Ensembles.
   C. Damage equipment used for Western Ensembles.
   D. Refuse all feedback on Western Ensembles.

9. Best practice when working on Setting Text to Music: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Setting Text to Music with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Damage equipment used for Setting Text to Music.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Setting Text to Music.
   D. Disrupt classmates during Setting Text to Music.

10. Best practice when working on Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble: (1 mark)
   A. Refuse all feedback on Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble.
   B. Practise Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   C. Damage equipment used for Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble.
   D. Disrupt classmates during Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble.

11. Best practice when working on Western Instruments: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Western Instruments with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Western Instruments.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Western Instruments.
   D. Damage equipment used for Western Instruments.

12. Best practice when working on Contemporary Songs from Kenya: (1 mark)
   A. Disrupt classmates during Contemporary Songs from Kenya.
   B. Refuse all feedback on Contemporary Songs from Kenya.
   C. Damage equipment used for Contemporary Songs from Kenya.
   D. Practise Contemporary Songs from Kenya with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Four-Part Harmony and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Music Notation Software. and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Dance Production and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Contemporary Songs from Kenya and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — Practise Instrumental Transpositions with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

2. C — Practise Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

3. D — The speed of the music

4. D — Practise Four-Part Harmony with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

5. B — Practise Rhythm with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

6. B — Practise Dance Production with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

7. A — Practise Music Notation Software. with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

8. A — Practise Western Ensembles with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

9. A — Practise Setting Text to Music with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

10. B — Practise Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

11. A — Practise Western Instruments with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

12. D — Practise Contemporary Songs from Kenya with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Four-Part Harmony; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Music Notation Software.; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Dance Production; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Contemporary Songs from Kenya; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
